Generated with Grok ImagineEvery software project starts simple.
You create a assets folder, add a few images, maybe an SVG logo, a custom font, and move on.
Weeks later, your project has evolved.
assets/
├── images/
├── icons/
├── svg/
├── fonts/
├── audio/
├── video/
└── lottie/At this point, managing assets starts becoming a problem that most teams simply accept. Developers manually import files. Asset registry files grow larger. Duplicate files creep into the project. Invalid filenames cause unexpected build failures. Merge conflicts become common because multiple developers modify the same asset registry. None of these tasks create business value. They’re repetitive maintenance.
That’s exactly the problem assets-toolkit was built to solve.
What is assets-toolkit?
assets-toolkit is an open-source CLI that automatically scans your project assets and generates clean, type-safe asset maps for:

• React Native

• Expo

• React

• Next.js

• Vite
Instead of manually maintaining asset imports, you simply run:
npx assets-toolkit generateWithin seconds, the toolkit scans your assets and generates strongly typed asset files that you can use throughout your application.
A Real-World Problem
Imagine you’re working on a project with several developers. One teammate adds new icons. Another renames a logo. A designer replaces a font. Someone else accidentally commits duplicate images. Now your manually maintained asset file is outdated.
export const images = {
logo: require("../assets/images/logo.png"),
profile: require("../assets/images/profile.png"),
home: require("../assets/images/home.png"),
// ...hundreds more
};Someone has to remember to update it. Again and again and again.
Over time, this file becomes another piece of code that requires constant maintenance.
A Better Approach
Instead of maintaining asset files by hand, let automation do the work.
Run one command:
npx assets-toolkit generateThe toolkit automatically:

• Scans your asset directories

• Detects supported asset types

• Preserves nested folder structures

• Generates type-safe asset maps

• Creates a centralized Assets object

• Reports duplicate assets

• Validates filenames before they become build problems
The generated output stays synchronized with your assets.
Before
Manual imports scattered throughout the application:
import logo from "../assets/images/logo.png";
import profile from "../assets/images/profile.png";
import search from "../assets/icons/search.svg";Or maintaining large registry files:
export const images = {
...
};After
Simply generate your assets:
npx assets-toolkit generateThen use:
import { Assets } from "./generated-assets";const logo = Assets.images.logo;
const search = Assets.svg.icons.search;
const font = Assets.fonts.Inter;The generated code stays organized, predictable, and type-safe.
More Than Asset Generation
While generating asset maps is the primary feature, real-world projects usually need much more.
That’s why assets-toolkit also includes tools to help keep your asset folders healthy.
Validate assets
npx assets-toolkit doctorDetects:

• Duplicate files

• Invalid filenames

• Missing asset folders

• Unsupported assets

• Large files
Automatically fix filename issues
npx assets-toolkit doctor --fixInstead of manually renaming files, the toolkit can safely rename invalid filenames and remove duplicates after confirmation.
Generate project reports
npx assets-toolkit reportsView useful information including:

• Asset counts

• Storage usage

• Largest files

• Extension breakdown

• Generated output status
Clean generated files
npx assets-toolkit cleanUseful when switching branches or regenerating assets from a clean state.
Why I Built It
Over the years, I’ve worked on multiple projects where asset management was handled manually.
Every project had some variation of the same problems:

• Large asset registry files

• Manual imports

• Duplicate assets

• Inconsistent filenames

• Time spent maintaining boilerplate
The solution wasn’t another document explaining best practices.
The solution was automation.
That’s why I built assets-toolkit.
The goal wasn’t to introduce another dependency.
The goal was to remove repetitive work from everyday development.
Supported Asset Types
The toolkit currently supports:

• Images

• SVG

• Fonts

• Audio

• Video

• Lottie animations
It also preserves your existing folder structure, making the generated output easy to understand and navigate.
Getting Started
Install it as a development dependency:
npm install --save-dev assets-toolkitGenerate your assets:
npx assets-toolkit generateThat’s all you need to get started.
Final Thoughts
Good developer tools don’t add complexity — they remove it.
Asset management shouldn’t require developers to manually maintain registry files, chase broken imports, or discover duplicate files during release day.
assets-toolkit automates those repetitive tasks so you can spend more time building features and less time maintaining boilerplate.
If you’re working with React Native, Expo, React, Next.js, or Vite, I’d love for you to give it a try and share your feedback.
Resources
📦 npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/assets-toolkit
⭐ GitHub: https://github.com/Mukthahar26/react-native-assets-toolkit
If you have ideas for new features or improvements, feel free to open an issue or start a discussion. Community feedback will help shape future releases.
Happy coding! 🚀
